records.summary: Long rests are more effective at night when the temperature is cooler. Characters without blankets or fire must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 13) to avoid exhaustion from the cold.

1.Travel Pace: •Slow: 1 mile per hour (advantage on Survival checks). •Normal: 2 miles per hour. •Fast: 3 miles per hour (disadvantage on Perception checks to spot dangers). 2.Navigation Difficulty: •Paths through the mountains are difficult to follow. Wisdom (Survival) checks (DC 15) are required every 4 hours to stay on course. A failed check results in the party becoming lost, adding 1d6 hours to the journey. 3.Climbing Rules: •Climbing cliffs or steep rock faces requires Strength (Athletics) checks (DC 14). Players climbing without proper equipment must make the checks every 10 feet or risk falling. •Falling characters take 1d6 bludgeoning damage per 10 feet of fall. Climbing companions can attempt to catch them with a Dexterity (Acrobatics) check (DC 15).

Finding a sheltered place for a short rest requires a successful Wisdom (Survival) check (DC 12). Without shelter, characters resting in high winds or cold temperatures must make a Constitution save (DC 13) or suffer one level of exhaustion.

1.Loose Boulder Traps: •Natural or placed by bandits, these traps send large rocks rolling down a slope. Players must make a Dexterity save (DC 14) or take 3d8 bludgeoning damage. 2.Concealed Cliffside Paths: •Some paths seem safe but end abruptly. A failed Wisdom (Perception) check (DC 15) can lead to a character falling from a hidden drop. 3.Bandit Ambushes: •Narrow mountain trails are ideal ambush spots. Roll a Wisdom (Perception) check (DC 15) to notice the ambush in time.
Effect: Gain proficiency in Survival. You can locate water and edible plants in desert environments with an Intelligence (Survival) check (DC 12).

Concealed by vegetation, these pits can drop characters 10 feet into rubble or water. •DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) to notice. Failing to spot them results in a fall and becoming restrained. 2.Rust Trap Wires: Thin wires set by scavenger gangs, meant to trip or injure intruders. •Dexterity saving throw (DC 13) or take 1d6 slashing damage and be knocked prone. 3.Snare Vines: Reactive vines ensnare those who step on them. •Strength saving throw (DC 14) or the character becomes restrained. Vines take 5 slashing damage to cut through.

Moving carelessly through ruins may result in injuries. Each hour spent in the ruins, characters roll a Dexterity saving throw (DC 12). On a failure, they take 1d4 slashing damage. 2.Collapsed Structures: Unstable buildings may collapse with little warning. Characters in or near unstable structures must make Dexterity saving throws (DC 14) to avoid falling debris (2d6 bludgeoning damage). 3.Diseases and Parasites: •Urban Plague: Caused by contact with contaminated water or surfaces. Constitution saving throw (DC 14) to avoid -2 to Constitution until cured. •Spores of Decay: Inhaled from moldy buildings or fungal overgrowth. Constitution save (DC 13); two failed saves result in the poisoned condition and mild hallucinations. 4.Hostile Flora: Certain plants entangle those who come too close. Characters caught in Strangle Vines must make a Strength saving throw (DC 13) or become restrained. Breaking free requires 5 slashing damage.

•Ash-Covered Paths: Moving through thick ash requires Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks (DC 12) to avoid slipping or sinking into unstable ground. •Ground Shifts: For every hour traveled, roll a d6. On a roll of 1, the ground shifts unexpectedly, requiring a Dexterity saving throw (DC 14) to avoid falling prone or sliding into fissures. 3.Climbing Burned Structures: •Charred trees or ruins can be used for vantage points, but they are unstable. Climbing requires Dexterity (Athletics) checks (DC 13), with a failure potentially resulting in a collapse and 2d6 bludgeoning damage from the fall.

•Swimming: Swimming in deep water requires Strength (Athletics) checks (DC 12) each hour or causes exhaustion. •Boats and Rafts: Improvised boats or rafts can help; however, navigating requires Dexterity (Vehicle Handling) checks (DC 13) to avoid hidden obstacles. •Unstable Structures: For each hour spent exploring buildings or structures, roll a d6. On a 1, the structure collapses, and each character inside must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 14) to avoid 2d6 bludgeoning damage from falling debris.

Scattered fires and hidden heat pockets remain active. Characters walking near these must succeed on Dexterity saving throws (DC 13) to avoid 1d6 fire damage. Prolonged exposure near heat pockets can also cause exhaustion from extreme heat.

•Heavy Rain: Reduces visibility to 20 feet, makes surfaces slippery, and increases water levels. Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks (DC 13) are required to avoid falling. •Fog: Lowers visibility to 15 feet and imposes disadvantage on Perception checks relying on sight. •Mosquito Swarms: Clouds of mosquitoes inflict 1 piercing damage every 10 minutes unless players have repellent or cover.
•Characters may need to bypass malfunctioning electronic doors or use emergency power to operate lifts. This requires Intelligence (Technology) checks (DC 15) or a manual override.

Spikes, broken glass, and other makeshift traps litter the highway, making it difficult for vehicles or people to travel without risk. These require Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks (DC 14) to avoid injury when moving quickly. 4.Weathered Roadblocks: Abandoned vehicles may form natural barricades, forcing travelers to climb over or find ways around. Some barricades have been reinforced by raiders or other survivors, creating a point of conflict.

Cracks and fissures may open suddenly, releasing steam or magma. For each hour in volcanic zones, roll a d6. On a roll of 1, a fissure opens nearby, requiring a Dexterity saving throw (DC 14) to avoid 2d6 fire damage from erupting steam or magma.

Describe distant sounds, such as the echo of footsteps or an id ling engine, to build suspense. Use limited visibility from dust, fog, or rain to create uncertainty around each encounter. 5.Encourage Problem-Solving: Players may need to clear roadblocks, build makeshift defenses, or set traps of their own to survive. Allow for creative solutions when navigating or defending their positions on the highway. This Skeletons of Highways guide provides everything players and GMs need to explore an abandoned highway filled with both opportunity and danger. The settingʼs open, vulnerable nature and unpredictable encounters make every stretch of road a new test of survival and ingenuity.

Some areas have hot springs with potential healing properties, while others release toxic steam. Identifying safe springs requires Wisdom (Survival) checks (DC 13). Failure results in exposure to poison (Constitution save, DC 13, or take 1d4 poison damage).

Occasional rain mixes with sulfur, creating acidic or scalding droplets. When caught in a rain, players must make Dexterity checks (DC 13) to find shelter quickly or take 1d4 acid damage each minute exposed.
Characters resting in unventilated rooms suffer the effects of contaminated air, requiring Constitution saving throws (DC 13) every two hours to avoid exhaustion.

1.Poisonous Ash Clouds: Pockets of poisonous ash create choking hazards. Characters exposed to these clouds must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 15) every 10 minutes or suffer 1 level of exhaustion.

1.Air Contamination: Stale air sometimes carries toxins or low oxygen levels. For each hour spent in a contaminated area, characters must succeed on Constitution saving throws (DC 14) or gain 1 level of exhaustion. 2.Power Shortages: The bunkerʼs power systems are unreliable. Roll a d6 every hour; on a roll of 1 or 2, the power fails temporarily, extinguishing all lights and shutting down electrical doors and ventilation for 1d10 minutes. 3.Structural Collapse: The bunker network is unstable in places. For every hour spent in a high-risk area, roll a d6. On a 1, parts of the tunnel or room collapse, requiring Dexterity saving throws (DC 15) to avoid 3d6 bludgeoning damage from falling debris. 4.Defunct Defense Systems: Some bunkers have malfunctioning defenses, such as automated turrets or laser traps. If triggered, players must make Dexterity saving throws (DC 14) to dodge attacks, taking 2d6 piercing or radiant damage on a failure.

1.Aquatic Mutants: Mutated animals, such as oversized fish, amphibians, or alligator-like creatures, prowl the flooded areas. They are highly territorial and may attack to defend their territory. 2.Scavenger Encampments: Small groups of survivors or scavengers may have set up makeshift floating camps. They could be willing to trade or hostile, depending on their outlook and the state of their resources. 3.Fishing and Trapping: Some scavengers have adapted to the flooded environment by setting traps for fish or game. Players may find these traps to collect food or encounter their makers, who may not appreciate the interference. 4.Collapsed Vehicle Pileup: Submerged cars or boats form a difficult barrier, hiding creatures or valuable supplies. Crossing requires Dexterity checks (DC 13) to avoid injury, while searching vehicles might yield tools or supplies. 5.Submerged Storage Cellars: Some homes have flooded basements containing relics or valuable items, though they are often buried under water and debris. Searching through these cellars may reveal valuables but also risks collapse.

1.Terrain Types: •Crumbling Ruins: Buildings reduced to rubble offer cover but may collapse at any time. Navigating these ruins requires a Dexterity (Acrobatics) check (DC 13) to avoid falling debris. •Radiation Hotspots: Invisible patches of intense radiation. A failed Constitution saving throw (DC 14) causes contamination, dealing 1d6 radiation damage per hour of exposure. •Toxic Swamps: Puddles of sludge and waste that corrode armor and flesh. Contact with toxic waste deals 1d8 acid damage, and the affected creature must make a Constitution save (DC 12) to avoid poisoning. •Ash Flats: Open plains coated in dust and debris, offering little cover. Windstorms can reduce visibility and make stealth nearly impossible. 2.Weather and Conditions: •Radioactive Storms: Roll a d20 every 8 hours; on a 5 or lower, a storm rolls in, causing acid rain and irradiating everything caught outside. Players must make Dexterity saving throws (DC 15) to find cover or take 2d6 acid damage per round. •

1.Radiation Poisoning: •Characters accumulate radiation points with exposure. Every 10 points require a Constitution saving throw (DC 14) or result in one level of exhaustion and 1d8 poison damage. •Radiation can be removed only through decontamination showers, anti-rad injections, or specialized medicine. 2.Toxic Gas Leaks: •Breathing in toxic gas forces a Constitution saving throw (DC 13). Failure causes 2d8 poison damage and inflicts the poisoned condition for 1d4 hours. Masks or air filtration gear can negate this hazard. 3.Collapsed Structures: •Any loud noise or vibration has a chance of triggering a building collapse. Characters within the area must succeed on Dexterity saving throws (DC 15) or take 3d10 bludgeoning damage. 4.Landmines: •Mines are buried beneath the ash or sand. A Wisdom (Perception) check (DC 14) detects them. If triggered, they deal 4d8 piercing damage in a 10-foot radius.

1.Waterborne Diseases: Exposure to contaminated water requires characters to roll a Constitution saving throw (DC 13) after each hour spent in the water. Failure results in contracting Sewer Fever, imposing -1 to Strength and Dexterity until cured. 2.Hidden Sinkholes: Sinkholes form beneath the water, causing sudden drops. Characters who encounter a sinkhole must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 14) or be pulled down 10 feet, requiring a Strength (Athletics) check (DC 13) to resurface.

1.Booby-Trapped Vehicles: Some vehicles were rigged to deter looters, containing hidden traps like broken glass, explosives, or alarms. Characters searching such a vehicle must succeed on Wisdom (Perception) checks (DC 13) to spot traps or Dexterity saving throws (DC 15) to avoid 2d6 piercing or fire damage. 2.Concealed Predators: Wild animals, mutated creatures, or desperate survivors may hide within vehicles. Characters searching these vehicles may encounter hostile creatures that attack with surprise. 3.Collapsing Vehicles: Many vehicles are rusted and unstable. Characters attempting to stand on or enter such a vehicle must make Dexterity saving throws (DC 13) to avoid falling or being injured by sharp metal, taking 1d6 slashing damage.

Long rests are challenging in the bunker and require a relatively secure room with working ventilation. For every hour of rest, a character on watch must make a Wisdom (Perception) check (DC 13) to detect approaching threats. Failure results in an ambush or hazard (such as a creature entering or a structural collapse).

1.Travel Pace: •Slow: 1 mile per hour (advantage on Perception and Stealth checks). •Normal: 2 miles per hour. •Fast: 3 miles per hour (disadvantage on Perception checks and increased chance of triggering hazards). 2.Navigation Difficulty: •Roads have crumbled, landmarks are obliterated, and strange topography makes it hard to navigate. Wisdom (Survival) checks (DC 15) are required every 4 hours to stay on course. A failed check adds 1d4 hours to the journey. •Geiger counters and other specialized equipment provide advantage on locating safe paths. 3.Resting and Shelter: •Finding secure shelter is crucial to avoid exposure to radiation and predators. A Wisdom (Survival) check (DC 13) can locate a usable ruin or bunker for short rests. Long rests without a sealed location expose players to random encounters or radiation poisoning.
Finding a safe place for a short rest requires a successful Wisdom (Survival) check (DC 12). Failure means no recovery due to environmental stress or predator encounters.

1.Rad Traps: •Bombs rigged with radioactive material explode when triggered, releasing a cloud of radiation. Characters within 15 feet must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC 14) or take 2d10 radiation damage and accumulate 5 radiation points. 2.Collapsed Roadways: •Roads and highways are cracked and broken. Any vehicle crossing these areas must succeed on a Dexterity (Vehicle Handling) check (DC 13) or become stuck or damaged. 3.Explosive Ruins: •Some buildings are rigged with explosives by scavengers or bandits. A failed Wisdom (Perception) check (DC 15) triggers the explosives, dealing 4d8 fire damage in a 20-foot radius.
Each hour of rest, each character on watch must make a Wisdom (Perception) check (DC 13) to notice approaching threats.
Effect: Gain proficiency in Investigation. You can locate useful materials or items in ruined buildings with a check (DC 10).
Effect: Gain proficiency in Survival. You can find edible plants and water sources in overgrown city environments with an Intelligence (Survival) check (DC 12).

•Sentient Oozes: Strange slimes that may offer information or alliances—if the players can communicate with them. •Gravekeeper's Ghost: A spirit that guards the catacombs. It may offer warnings or aid in exchange for offerings. •

•Some sections have flood gates that release rushing water or sewage. Dexterity saves (DC 15) are required to avoid being swept away or trapped. 3.Collapsed Tunnels: •Disturbing fragile walls or making loud noises may trigger a collapse. Dexterity saves (DC 14) avoid 3d6 bludgeoning damage from falling debris. 4.Diseased Swarms: •Rats, insects, or bats swarm intruders, spreading disease. Players exposed must make Constitution saves (DC 13) or suffer from a debilitating illness.
•Crossing through sewage or stagnant water imposes exhaustion without protective gear. Constitution saving throws (DC 12) every hour prevent disease or exhaustion levels from accumulating.
•Some areas require climbing slick walls or scaling corroded ladders. Dexterity (Acrobatics) or Strength (Athletics) checks (DC 13) are needed to avoid falling.

•A group of lost adventurers or miners begs the party for help. They may offer supplies or information but could also lead the players into a trap. 4.The Creatureʼs Lair: •The players stumble upon a powerful creatureʼs den—such as a giant spider queen or a cave drake. They must either fight, sneak past, or attempt to negotiate with the creature. 5.The Ancient Altar: •Deep in the cavern lies an ancient altar with strange runes. Activating it may grant boons—or awaken dangerous spirits.

•Some tunnels end abruptly in deep chasms. A failed Perception check (DC 12) results in a fall. Characters must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 15) to catch themselves or suffer falling damage (1d6 per 10 feet). 4.Poisonous Fungi: •Touching or disturbing certain fungi releases spores. Players in the area must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC 13) or take 2d6 poison damage and become blinded for 1d4 rounds.

•Cold Caves: Characters without proper gear must make Constitution saving throws (DC 12) every hour or suffer 1 level of exhaustion. •Stale Air Pockets: In deeper caves, the air may become thin and stale. After 1 hour, players must make Constitution saving throws (DC 13) each hour or become fatigued. •Poisonous Gas Pockets: Some caves contain invisible toxic gas. A failed Constitution saving throw (DC 14) results in 2d8 poison damage and the poisoned condition for 1 hour.

•An altar offers a boon to those who perform a specific ritual—but performing it incorrectly triggers a curse. A successful Religion check (DC 13) reveals the correct method. 4.Collapsing Ceiling: •Activating the wrong lever or disturbing a fragile section of the temple causes the ceiling to collapse. Players must make Dexterity saves (DC 14) or take 4d6 bludgeoning damage and become restrained. 5.The Spiritʼs Trial: •A benevolent or vengeful spirit offers the players a challenge. If they succeed, they gain a blessing or vital information—if they fail, they suffer consequences such as temporary ability score reductions.
